notes: Follow-up after inspecting timing-pilot/v2: exploratory, one predeclared dataset per size, three new inference seeds; not confirmatory.

Primary strong scaling fixes 512 particles, 32 temperatures and 10 MH proposals per particle per stage across 1/8/32/64 ranks. Proposal totals must match; graph quality and PIP differences across core counts are measured, not assumed invariant.
All ranks execute identical fixed-work SMC settings; adaptive 512/1024-particle SMC at 64 ranks is a separately labelled quality arm, not silently substituted for fixed-work scaling.

MCMC uses independent chains per core, with loop budgets 0.5/2/10/30/120 seconds and an extra 480 seconds at 64 ranks. Measured inference time includes summaries and aggregation, not just the nominal loop budget.
All compared methods and budgets run on the same exclusive node within each dataset/seed bundle, in a frozen random order. Report active and reserved costs.

Graph recovery is assessed against synthetic truth, independent of any MCMC convergence gate. Edge-probability differences to long MCMC are empirical agreement, not posterior error for large networks.
Exact posterior PIP error remains available at d=12; prior larger-network reference failures remain disclosed in the earlier pilot and are not reclassified as passed.

Descriptive recovery targets use the mean recovery of all three 64-rank 480-second MCMC runs: directed and skeleton F1 no more than 0.02 below, SHD/true-edge-count no more than 0.05 above. Both methods must qualify in every seed. No formal noninferiority or universal speed claim.

A four-hour step cap is fixed before the new fits. All attempts and timeouts are retained; previous single-core adaptive timeouts are not overwritten. No new long-reference jobs or sampler/model/default changes.
